decisive_items: She had been diagnosed with a tenosynovial giant cell tumor by MRI at a local hospital
a neoplastic lesion remained in the differential
Post-contrast images demonstrated homogeneous enhancement of the tendons and synovial membrane, supporting synovial hyperplasia
response.rationale: R6 is most likely because the patient had a prior MRI diagnosis of tenosynovial giant cell tumor, and current imaging shows an enhancing tendon-sheath/synovial lesion with restricted diffusion and median nerve compression, with a neoplastic lesion still in the differential. The other candidates are preliminary or secondary findings rather than the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Median nerve compression is secondary to the mass; atypical carpal tunnel syndrome was only a preliminary diagnosis.
Tenosynovitis is a descriptive finding; the enhancing tendon sheath lesion with restricted diffusion and prior TGCT diagnosis favors a neoplastic process.
Synovitis/synovial hyperplasia is a feature of the lesion, not the specific diagnosis; prior TGCT diagnosis is more specific.
Degenerative carpal bone changes are incidental and do not explain the tendon sheath mass or median nerve compression.
